newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Group Five profit set to swell, eyes world.
newsitem.headline: Group Five profit set to swell, eyes world.

text.p: South African construction to engineering firm Group Five Ltd plans to treble its earnings by the end of the century and was eyeing international ventures, its directors said on Friday.
"We hope to treble the size of the company by 2000 in terms of earnings," financial director Howard Turner said.
But the current financial year to end-June profits would be squeezed due to high interest rates, which are choking the residential properties and building divisions, he said.

"We have a concern about this year. Last year's rate hike has adversely affected residential properties and building in the short-term. In the year to June we won't reach our previous earnings per share figure due to the share issue," Turner said.
This, he added, would likely affect the company's current four times dividend cover.

Group Five increased its number of shares to 73 million from 42 million previously. Its earnings per share figure for the year to June 1996 was 83.8 cents and attributable profit was 35.03 million rand.
Newly appointed chief executive Mike Lomas told a media briefing that Group Five was positively placed for the future and was eyeing international opportunities to help it grow.

"We've set our growth objective for the year 2000 and we're going to stick to that. There are some opportunities that we want to pursue that are related to our existing businesses and would help us grow our existing business," Lomas said.
He saw these opportunities being seized within six to 12 months but declined to give further details, beyond saying that they would be "substantially important."

Lomas said Group Five did not plan to head down an acquisitive path but would rather take advantage of existing business opportunities. He said building toll roads was an example of the kind of projects the group was looking at.
Group Five's aim was to become a blue-chip company and would likely move beyond Africa within five years.
"We are looking internationally but we're doing it very cautiously. We have contacts outside the country and we'll pursue that...probably in less than five years," Lomas said.
Its current African interests were performing well and would contribute more than 10 percent to turnover this year.
"The gateway to Africa is going to help us quite a lot. There's great potential in Africa," Lomas said.

Lomas was appointed chief executive with immediate effect on Thursday. Formerly managing director of Group Five's engineering division, he replaces Theunis Kotzee who resigned on May 13 following policy differences with the board.
"This trauma that we've gone through over the last few weeks has brought the team closer together. It was dynamic. It has not affected the performance of the group at all," Lomas said.
